premise: The forest wakes one sound at a time, from the first drip of dew to the sun reaching the tallest branch.
inspiration: Cumulative waking-song folk pattern (The House That Jack Built), turned into a dawn roll call of sounds: one drop, two, three, a voice, an answer, the wind, the sun.
lesson: Mornings arrive a little at a time, and every small sound is part of it.

en-US.title: The Forest Wakes Up
en-US.text: {tree:sway loop 0.3} {flower:sway loop 0.4} Shh. The forest is still asleep. Listen. Drip. One drop of dew slides off a leaf. Drip, drop. Two drops. Drip, drop, plip. Three! The ground goes hmm, and the moss goes hmm, and a fern uncurls, slow as a yawn. {bird:hop x2} Tweet! A small voice tries out the morning. Tweet, tweet! A second voice answers. The wind sits up and {tree:sway 0.6} rustles the tall trees, rustle, rustle, hello, hello. Now the sun puts one finger over the hill. It touches the grass, {flower:glow} it touches the flowers, it touches the very {tree:glow hold} top of the tallest tree. Every leaf goes gold. Can you hear it? The whole forest is humming. Good morning, forest. Good morning, you.

es-ES.title: El bosque se despierta
es-ES.text: {tree:sway loop 0.3} {flower:sway loop 0.4} Chist. El bosque todavía duerme. Escucha. Plic. Una gota de rocío resbala por una hoja. Plic, ploc. Dos gotas. Plic, ploc, plin. ¡Tres! El suelo dice mmm, y el musgo dice mmm, y un helecho se estira despacio, como un bostezo. {bird:hop x2} ¡Pío! Una voz pequeña prueba la mañana. ¡Pío, pío! Otra voz le contesta. El viento se despereza y {tree:sway 0.6} mece los árboles altos, susurra que susurra, hola, hola. Ahora el sol asoma un dedo por la colina. Toca la hierba, {flower:glow} toca las flores, toca la punta {tree:glow hold} más alta del árbol más alto. Cada hoja se vuelve de oro. ¿Lo oyes? El bosque entero está tarareando. Buenos días, bosque. Buenos días a ti.

sound.note: single soft water drops, one, then two, then three
two small bird chirps answering each other
